comment: Release conditions for every exact-pinned version in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies and overrides),
plus any override added to clear an npm audit advisory. An exact pin is invisible to update-npm-deps.ps1 - that
script upgrades caret ranges and skips exact versions - so nothing would ever remind you a pin is stale. This file
is what makes that check happen: on every run the script executes each `check` and compares its trimmed stdout to
`expect`. Equal means the pin is still required; different means the condition that justified the pin has changed
and the pin should be re-examined. `check: null` means no mechanical test exists - it is reported for manual review
on every run instead of going quiet. Every exact pin must have an entry here, and every entry must name a package
that is actually present in the declared section; the script reports either mismatch.

@codemirror/state.why: obsidian's peerDependencies names this exact version. A second copy in the tree means two CodeMirror state instances at runtime, so editor extensions would attach to the wrong one.

@codemirror/view.why: Same as @codemirror/state - obsidian peer-pins it exactly, and the view layer must run against Obsidian's own CodeMirror instance.

moment.why: Must match the copy Obsidian bundles and re-exports as `moment`: obsidian's own dependencies name this exact version, and a different one would type against an API the runtime does not have.

js-yaml.why: Astro and Starlight `import yaml from 'js-yaml'`, and js-yaml 5 is ESM-only with NO default export - hoisting 5.x into their subtree makes `astro build` die on 'The requested module js-yaml does not provide an export named default' before it reads a single page. The override exists to keep the whole tree off the vulnerable 3.x line and off 4.3.1 and below, which sit inside GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh (maxTotalMergeKeys does not limit CPU use for empty merge sources); 4.3.2 is the patched release on the v4-legacy dist-tag, so it clears the advisory while staying loadable. The check records the range astro itself asks for: when astro moves to 5.x, this pin can be dropped.

smol-toml.why: markdownlint-cli2 pins smol-toml at exactly 1.7.0 and astro / @astrojs/internal-helpers ask for ^1.6.0, so the whole tree deduped onto 1.7.0 - which is inside GHSA-7w5x-hrqm-74c2 (<=1.7.0: denial of service via malformed TOML documents). Both dependents are already on their newest release, so nothing here can be bumped to fix it, and npm audit only offers --force down to markdownlint-cli2@0.21.0, i.e. a downgrade. 1.8.0 is the patched line and is already resolved separately in this same tree under cspell-config-lib, so the override clears the advisory without moving anything onto an API its dependents do not use. Exact rather than caret so the sweep cannot float it onto a future 2.x that markdownlint-cli2 exact pin would reject. The check records the version markdownlint-cli2 itself asks for: when it moves onto a patched smol-toml, this override can be dropped.

fflate.why: satori pins fflate at exactly 0.7.3, which sits inside GHSA-px8p-9vwx-vf98 (0.7.0 - 0.7.4: unzipSync can enter an infinite loop on a malformed ZIP64 archive). npm audit's only offer is `--force` down to satori@0.32.0, i.e. a downgrade. 0.7.5 is the patched release on the same minor - and is already what @shuding/opentype.js resolves to in this same tree - so the override clears the advisory without moving satori off the fflate API it pins itself to. The check records the version satori itself asks for: when satori moves onto a patched fflate, this override can be dropped.

obsidian.why: These mocks reproduce one specific Obsidian API surface, so the type definitions they are written against are pinned rather than floated. The check records the newest published obsidian release: when it moves, the mocks should be re-examined against the new API rather than silently drifting.

typescript.why: TypeScript 7 (tsgo) breaks this toolchain: @typescript-eslint's parser crashes on the native API, so type-aware ESLint cannot run on 7. @typescript-eslint peer-requires the range below, so 6.x is the last usable major. Hold until obsidian-dev-utils migrates.
